## Kronos — Environment, Health & Safety (open, CC BY 4.0)
The Kronos environment, health, and safety case — low-neutron, meltdown-proof, no long-lived waste, and almost no water — plus one honest look at the world fusion makes possible.
Design figures are computed and reproducible; nothing here is economics or an offer of securities.

### The Safety Case
- [AI Control Beneath Deterministic Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/ai-control-safety-interlocks.html): Advanced control keeps the plasma burning, but safety never depends on it — simple fail-safe interlocks sit above the AI layer.
- [ALARA and Worker Dose](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/worker-dose-alara.html): Occupational dose is kept As Low As Reasonably Achievable through shielding, remote work, time, distance, and monitoring.
- [Beryllium Handling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/beryllium-handling.html): Beryllium can serve as a neutron multiplier in the breeder blanket; its dust is toxic and is controlled by containment and respiratory protection.
- [Breeder Blanket Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/lithium-breeder-blanket-safety.html): The lithium-bearing blanket breeds tritium and is reactive with water; it is handled in inert, contained, and monitored systems.
- [Burn-Condition Fragility](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/burn-condition-fragility.html): Fusion burn requires many parameters held simultaneously in a narrow window; losing any one ends the burn.
- [Burner Plug Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/burner-plug-safety.html): The tandem-mirror plugs confine plasma with high field; if plug performance drops, the plasma leaks out and the burn ends — a safe direction.
- [Chemical and Material Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/chemical-safety.html): The plant's chemical hazards — lithium, beryllium, coolants — are conventional industrial hazards managed by standard practice.
- [Control-System and Interlock Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/control-system-safety.html): Safety interlocks are deterministic and fail-safe: on any fault or loss of signal, the machine drives itself to a safe state.
- [Cryogenic Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/cryogenic-safety.html): Superconducting coils run near absolute zero; the hazards are cold burns, pressure from boil-off, and oxygen displacement — all standard cryogenic risks.
- [Decay Heat and Passive Cooling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/decay-heat-and-cooling.html): After shutdown the residual heat comes from activated structure, is small, and is removed without powered cooling.
- [Defense in Depth](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/defense-in-depth.html): Independent barriers and layered systems mean no single failure can produce a significant release.
- [Deuterium Handling Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/deuterium-safety.html): Deuterium is a stable, non-radioactive hydrogen isotope; its only notable hazard is flammability, handled by standard gas practice.
- [Direct Energy Conversion Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/burner-direct-conversion-safety.html): The burner converts charged-particle energy straight to electricity, so its hazards are electrical — and it needs almost no water.
- [Disruptions and Plasma Quench](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/plasma-quench.html): A disruption ends the plasma abruptly; its loads are engineered for, and it removes rather than adds energy to the reaction.
- [Fire and Explosion Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fire-safety.html): The flammable inventory is small quantities of hydrogen isotopes; standard hydrogen-safety practice controls the risk, with no radiological coupling.
- [Fusion vs Fission: A Safety Scorecard](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/safety-vs-fission-comparison.html): Graded on the same ruler, fusion clears the defining fission safety hazards — not by better operation, but by their absence.
- [Hazard Categorization vs Fission](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/hazard-categorization.html): Categorizing a plant by its actual hazards places fusion well below fission, because the defining fission hazards are absent.
- [Helium-3 Handling Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/helium-3-safety.html): Helium-3 is a stable, non-radioactive, inert gas — the burner's fuel poses no radiological handling hazard.
- [High-Field Safety Zones](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/high-field-safety.html): Very strong static magnetic fields require controlled zones for magnetic objects and implants, a purely physical precaution.
- [Loss-of-Coolant Response](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/loss-of-coolant-response.html): With no large decay-heat source, losing coolant does not lead to core damage — the structure stays below its limits passively.
- [Loss-of-Power Response](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/loss-of-power-response.html): A total station blackout ends the fusion reaction rather than threatening it, because confinement and heating need power to continue.
- [Low-Activation Material Choices](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/low-activation-materials.html): Choosing materials that form only short-lived radioisotopes is the design decision that gives fusion its clean waste profile.
- [Magnet Quench Protection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/quench-protection.html): A quench is detected in milliseconds and the coil's energy is dumped to external resistors before local heating can cause damage.
- [Magnetic Field Worker Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/magnetic-field-worker-safety.html): Static magnetic fields are managed with exposure zoning, implant screening, and projectile control — established strong-magnet practice.
- [Neutron Activation Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/neutron-activation-safety.html): Neutrons make nearby structures mildly and temporarily radioactive; low-activation materials keep the effect small and short-lived.
- [Neutron Radiation Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/neutron-radiation-safety.html): 14 MeV fusion neutrons are shielded during operation, and they vanish the instant the plasma stops — there is no residual neutron field.
- [No Basis for Large Off-Site Evacuation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-evacuation-planning-basis.html): With a bounded, tritium-limited source term, protective actions stay largely on-site — there is no large-zone evacuation basis.
- [No Chain Reaction, No Criticality](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-chain-reaction.html): Fusion has no neutron multiplication feedback, so the concept of criticality — central to fission safety — does not apply.
- [No Fissile Material](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-fissile-material.html): There is no uranium, plutonium, or enriched fuel anywhere in a Kronos plant — the entire fissile hazard class is absent.
- [Passive Safety by Physics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/passive-safety-by-physics.html): Kronos safety leans first on inherent physical behavior, then on passive systems, and only last on active controls.
- [Permeation Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-permeation.html): Material choices, coatings, and negative-pressure design slow tritium migration through walls to keep it inside the loop.
- [Post-Shutdown Radiation Fields](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/gamma-and-decay-heat.html): After shutdown the only radiation comes from activated structure and decays quickly, allowing controlled access on human timescales.
- [Proliferation Resistance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/proliferation-resistance.html): Fusion uses no fissile material, needs no enrichment, and produces no plutonium — removing the classic weapons pathways.
- [Radiological Area Classification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/radiological-classification.html): Areas are zoned by radiation and contamination level, with access, monitoring, and protection scaled to each zone.
- [Remote Maintenance and Handling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/remote-maintenance-safety.html): Activated in-vessel components are serviced by remote handling, keeping workers out of the highest-dose regions entirely.
- [Right-Sized Emergency Preparedness](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/emergency-preparedness.html): Emergency provisions match the real hazard: on-site response and monitoring, not large off-site evacuation zones.
- [Seismic and External Hazards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/seismic-and-external-events.html): Earthquakes and external events can damage equipment, but the reaction ends on any upset and there is no large source to release.
- [Stored Magnetic Energy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/stored-magnetic-energy.html): The coils hold large electromagnetic energy that is removed on a fault by a controlled dump rather than an uncontrolled release.
- [Superconducting Magnet Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/magnet-safety-overview.html): The magnets store large energy and operate at high field and low temperature; their hazards are engineered, not radiological.
- [The Bounding Accident Source Term](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-accident-source-term.html): The most that any accident can release is set by the site tritium inventory — a small, well-characterized quantity.
- [The Byproduct-Material Framework](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/byproduct-material-framework.html): Because fusion handles radioactive material without fissile fuel or a chain reaction, it fits the byproduct-material regulatory framework.
- [The Confinement Barriers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/safety-barriers.html): Multiple physical boundaries stand between the tritium inventory and the environment, each independently effective.
- [The Density Limit as a Self-Limit](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/density-limit.html): Push plasma density too high and radiation losses cool the plasma — a built-in ceiling that prevents excursions.
- [The Kronos Safety Case in One Page](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/safety-overview.html): Fusion is safe not because of what operators do, but because of what the plasma physically cannot do.
- [The Licensing Pathway](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/licensing-pathway.html): Kronos pursues early, transparent engagement with the regulator to align on framework, hazards, and the safety basis before applying.
- [The Maximum Credible Accident](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/worst-case-analysis.html): Even the bounding beyond-design accident releases only a fraction of a small tritium inventory, with limited off-site consequence.
- [The Off-Normal Event Catalog](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/off-normal-events.html): Every credible upset — plasma disruption, loss of power, coolant loss, magnet fault, leak — resolves toward a safe, bounded state.
- [The Physics of Self-Limiting Burn](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/physics-of-self-limiting.html): The reaction rate depends so steeply on plasma conditions that any drift out of the operating window suppresses it.
- [The Small-Fuel-Inventory Principle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/small-fuel-inventory.html): At any instant only grams of fuel are inside the chamber, so the maximum energy the reaction can release is intrinsically small.
- [Tritium Handling and Containment](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-handling.html): Tritium is processed in sealed, negative-pressure systems with getters, permeation barriers, and continuous cleanup.
- [Tritium Inventory](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-inventory.html): The plant tritium inventory is small, tracked precisely, and held in engineered containment rather than in the plasma.
- [Tritium Monitoring and Detection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-monitoring.html): Continuous monitors on air, water, and stack streams catch any tritium migration before it can accumulate or escape.
- [Tritium Safeguards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-and-proliferation.html): Tritium is accounted for and physically secured, but alone it cannot produce a nuclear yield — the fissile pathway is still absent.
- [Tritium's Radiological Profile](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-biology.html): Tritium emits only weak beta radiation that cannot penetrate skin; the concern is intake, which handling controls address.
- [Vacuum Vessel Integrity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/vacuum-vessel-integrity.html): The vacuum vessel is the primary structural boundary; its failure de-confines the plasma and ends the reaction inward.
- [Why Fusion Cannot Melt Down](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/cannot-melt-down.html): A meltdown needs a large heat source that persists after shutdown. A fusion plasma has almost none.
- [Why Fusion Cannot Run Away](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/cannot-run-away.html): A runaway needs positive feedback on the reaction rate. Fusion has negative feedback, so excursions quench themselves.

### Low-Neutron & Waste
- [Activation Decay Timescales](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/activation-decay-timescales.html): The waste class of a fusion component is set by how fast its activation decays after shutdown, from hours to a few decades.
- [Activation Products: An Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/activation-products-overview.html): Neutron activation turns some structural atoms radioactive; which nuclides form, and how long they last, decides the waste class.
- [Activation in the Breeder (Hyperion)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/activation-in-the-breeder.html): The breeder's high 14 MeV flux activates its first wall and blanket the most; low-activation steel keeps that activation short-lived.
- [Activation in the Burner (Aegis / MetroVolt)](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/activation-in-the-burner.html): With only a 5.44% neutron channel, the burner activates far less structure than the breeder; charged-particle handling dominates instead.
- [Avoiding the Problem Elements](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/avoiding-problem-elements.html): A short list of elements — Nb, Mo, Ni, Co, Cu, Ag — produces most long-lived activation; excluding them is the core design rule.
- [Beryllium and Blanket Waste](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/beryllium-and-blanket-waste.html): Neutron multipliers and breeder materials form their own waste streams — activated but recyclable, with beryllium requiring toxic-dust control.
- [Breeder vs Burner: The Neutron Comparison](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/neutron-fraction-comparison.html): Two Kronos machines sit at opposite ends of the neutron scale: the breeder is neutron-rich by design, the burner is low-neutron.
- [Clearance and Free Release](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/clearance-and-free-release.html): Material whose activity falls below regulatory thresholds can clear for recycling or unrestricted reuse; much of fusion's mass eventually qualifies.
- [Decay Heat from Activation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/decay-heat-from-activation.html): Activation produces some decay heat, but far too little to threaten fuel integrity — there is no fuel to melt in the first place.
- [Decommissioning Waste](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/decommissioning-waste.html): At end of life the machine itself becomes the waste inventory — activated structure that, after decay, is largely recyclable or clearable.
- [First-Wall Neutron Loading](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/first-wall-neutron-loading.html): The first wall takes the full neutron flux; its loading, in MW per square meter, sets damage rate and replacement cadence.
- [Fuel Inventory vs Waste Inventory](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fuel-inventory-vs-waste-inventory.html): Fusion holds grams of fuel and generates its waste in the structure; fission holds tonnes of fuel that itself becomes the waste.
- [Fusion vs Fission Waste: An Honest Comparison](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-fission-waste-honest.html): Fusion produces no high-level waste and no actinides, but it does produce activated material and tritium — both statements are true.
- [Gamma Dose After Shutdown](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/gamma-dose-after-shutdown.html): The residual gamma field from short-lived activation sets how soon and how closely people can work near a shut-down machine.
- [Hands-On vs Remote Recycling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/hands-on-vs-remote-recycling.html): Whether recycling can be done by hand or must be done remotely depends on residual dose — and therefore on decay time and material choice.
- [How Neutron Activation Works](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/how-activation-works.html): A stable nucleus absorbs a neutron and becomes a different, often radioactive isotope; the reaction type and cross-section set the outcome.
- [Impurity Control in Structural Alloys](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/impurity-control-in-alloys.html): Parts-per-million of the wrong element can set the waste class; controlling impurities is a nuclear specification, not a metallurgical nicety.
- [Interim Storage and Decay](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/interim-storage-and-decay.html): On-site decay storage lets short-lived activation fade, converting most of the initial inventory into recyclable or clearable material.
- [LLW, ILW, and HLW Explained](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/llw-vs-ilw-vs-hlw.html): The three waste tiers differ in activity, heat, and required isolation time; fusion sits in the lowest, with no high-level tier.
- [Low-Neutron and Waste: A Glossary](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/waste-and-neutron-glossary.html): Plain definitions for the terms used across this section, from activation and clearance to dpa and transuranics.
- [Low-Neutron, Not Aneutronic](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/low-neutron-not-aneutronic.html): We hold a firm line on language: D-³He fusion is low-neutron. Any claim of zero neutrons would be false.
- [Material Selection Tradeoffs](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/material-selection-tradeoffs.html): No single material wins on every axis; the choice balances activation, high-temperature strength, and manufacturing maturity.
- [Neutron Energy Spectra of the Two Machines](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/neutron-energy-spectra.html): Neutron damage depends on energy: the breeder's 14.1 MeV neutrons and the burner's mixed 2.45/14.1 MeV output behave very differently.
- [Neutron Fluence, dpa, and Material Damage](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/neutron-fluence-and-damage.html): Cumulative neutron exposure is measured in displacements per atom; it drives both activation and the end-of-life of components.
- [Neutron Shielding Basics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/neutron-shielding-basics.html): Neutrons carry no charge, so fields cannot deflect them; they are slowed and absorbed by mass, in layers chosen to minimize activation.
- [No Actinides, No Transuranics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-actinides-no-transuranics.html): Without uranium in the machine, fusion breeds no plutonium or other actinides — the source of fission's longest-lived, most toxic waste.
- [No High-Level Waste](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-high-level-waste.html): Fusion generates no heat-producing, long-lived high-level waste, because it has no fissile fuel and no actinide inventory.
- [No Long-Lived Radiotoxicity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-long-lived-radiotoxicity.html): Fusion's waste loses its hazard on human timescales because it contains no actinides; the radiotoxicity does not persist for millennia.
- [No Spent Fuel](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-spent-fuel.html): Fusion never accumulates spent fuel: it burns grams of hydrogen isotopes, leaving helium and neutrons, not a growing rod inventory.
- [Recycling Activated Material](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/recycling-activated-material.html): Much activated fusion metal can be recycled after decay — within the nuclear sector or, once cleared, into ordinary supply chains.
- [Reduced-Activation Ferritic-Martensitic Steel](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/reduced-activation-ferritic-steel.html): RAFM steel swaps out the elements that make long-lived waste, giving a structural steel whose activation decays on human timescales.
- [Repository Timescales Compared](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/repository-timescales-compared.html): Fission's waste drives repository designs for tens of thousands of years; fusion's activated waste is bounded by decades to centuries.
- [Short-Lived vs Long-Lived Activation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/short-lived-vs-long-lived-activation.html): The dividing line in fusion waste is half-life: short-lived nuclides dominate early dose, a few long-lived ones dominate disposal.
- [Silicon-Carbide Composites](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/silicon-carbide-composites.html): SiC/SiC composites activate to very short-lived products and tolerate high temperature, though their manufacturing maturity still lags the metals.
- [The Breeder's 14 MeV Neutron Flux](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/breeder-14-mev-neutron-flux.html): Hyperion is a D-T machine: about 80% of its 88.7 MW fusion power leaves as 14.1 MeV neutrons that breed tritium and drive activation.
- [The Burner's 5.44% Neutron Fraction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/neutron-fraction-explained.html): The D-³He burner is low-neutron, not aneutronic: about 5.44% of its fusion energy leaves as neutrons in this design.
- [The Dominant Activation Nuclides](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/dominant-activation-nuclides.html): A short list of nuclides carries most of the dose and most of the long-term concern; naming them focuses the material design.
- [The Lithium Blanket at End-of-Life](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/lithium-blanket-end-of-life.html): A spent breeding blanket is recovered for its tritium and recyclable materials, not disposed of as a monolithic high-level object.
- [The Low-Activation Materials Strategy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/low-activation-materials-strategy.html): Choosing materials whose activation is short-lived is the single most powerful lever on the fusion waste class.
- [The Products Are Helium and Neutrons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/products-are-helium-and-neutrons.html): Fusion's direct products are inert helium and neutrons — not a spectrum of radioactive fission fragments locked in fuel.
- [Transmutation and the Nuclides It Creates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/transmutation-and-nuclides.html): Neutron capture and knock-out reactions transmute one element into another; the resulting nuclide chart is the fusion waste inventory.
- [Tritiated Waste Streams](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritiated-waste-streams.html): Materials that absorb tritium form a distinct waste stream, managed by outgassing and decay rather than by long-term disposal.
- [Tritium: Fuel, Not Waste](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-as-fuel-not-waste.html): Tritium is a radioactive fuel to be bred, stored, and burned — managed as a controlled inventory, not accumulated as waste.
- [Tungsten as a Plasma-Facing Material](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tungsten-plasma-facing.html): Tungsten armors the surfaces facing the plasma; it resists heat and erosion and activates to mostly short- and medium-lived products.
- [Vanadium Alloys](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/vanadium-alloys.html): Vanadium-chromium-titanium alloys offer low activation and high-temperature strength, with compatibility and impurity challenges.
- [Waste Class by Material](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/waste-classification-by-material.html): Each candidate structural material maps to a characteristic waste outcome; the mapping is how design choices become disposal outcomes.
- [Waste Classification: An Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/waste-classification-overview.html): Radioactive waste is sorted by how concentrated and how long-lived its activity is; fusion's inventory lands overwhelmingly in the lowest classes.
- [Waste Volume and the Main Streams](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/waste-volume-and-streams.html): Fusion waste splits into a few well-defined streams; knowing each one keeps the account honest and the totals modest.
- [What Fusion Waste Is Not](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/what-fusion-waste-is-not.html): Clearing up common misconceptions: fusion waste is not spent fuel, not high-level, not actinide-bearing, and not permanent.
- [What Fusion Waste Still Requires](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/what-fusion-waste-still-requires.html): Fusion waste is favorable, not free: it demands material control, decay storage, remote handling, tritium management, and real disposal.
- [Where the Burner's Neutrons Come From](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/where-the-neutrons-come-from.html): The burner's 5.44% neutron output comes from D-D side reactions and the D-T that D-D breeding feeds, not from the main D-³He channel.
- [Why Neutrons Drive the Waste Story](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/why-neutrons-matter-for-waste.html): Fusion has no spent fuel; nearly all of its radioactive waste is material activated by neutrons, so neutron budget is waste budget.

### Water, Land & Resources
- [Aegis Siting Context](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/aegis-siting-context.html): Aegis is the burner in a fixed defense-installation housing, sited on secured ground and generating power on-site.
- [Availability and Siting Honesty](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/availability-and-siting-honesty.html): The burner's studied availability is well short of hyperscale Tier III, so its siting value is water and land, not sole-source uptime.
- [Beryllium as a Neutron Multiplier](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/beryllium-neutron-multiplier.html): Some breeding-blanket designs use beryllium to multiply neutrons; beryllium supply and handling are the honest constraints.
- [Blanket and Coolant Materials](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/blanket-and-coolant-materials.html): The breeding blanket carries both breeding materials and a coolant; the coolant choice affects water use and materials footprint.
- [Capacity Density Versus Diffuse Sources](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/capacity-density-versus-diffuse-sources.html): Concentrated and diffuse generators occupy land in fundamentally different ways; each fits different sites and purposes.
- [Closed-Loop Cooling Systems](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/closed-loop-cooling-systems.html): Closed cooling loops recirculate a fixed inventory, rejecting heat to air or a small makeup stream rather than continuously withdrawing water.
- [Co-Located Generation and Transmission Land](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/colocated-generation-and-transmission-land.html): Generating power where it is consumed avoids the land and losses of long transmission corridors.
- [Comparing Water Intensity Fairly](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/comparing-water-intensity-fairly.html): A defensible water comparison fixes the metric, the boundary, and the life-cycle scope before any technology is ranked.
- [Concrete and Construction Materials](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/concrete-and-construction-materials.html): Foundations and shielding use concrete; it is the largest bulk material and its embodied footprint is a standard construction consideration.
- [Copper and Structural Materials](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/copper-and-structural-materials.html): Steel, copper, and specialized alloys make up most of a plant's mass; these are common, recyclable materials, not exotic scarcities.
- [Data-Center Cooling and the Water Context for MetroVolt](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/data-center-cooling-water-context.html): Large data centers consume water both directly for cooling and indirectly through the thermoelectric grid that powers them; on-site generation touches both.
- [Decommissioning and Land Restoration](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/decommissioning-and-land-restoration.html): A compact plant with a bounded material inventory is straightforward to decommission and return its land to other use.
- [Defensible Claims and Rejected Comparisons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/defensible-claims-and-rejected-comparisons.html): This repo publishes only solid, public, mechanism-based environmental claims; a scale-mismatched 'cleaner than X' comparison was rejected.
- [Deuterium from Water](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/deuterium-from-water.html): Deuterium, a fuel for both machines, is separated from ordinary water and is effectively unlimited at any plausible deployment scale.
- [Drought-Resilient Siting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/drought-resilient-siting.html): A generator that does not depend on a large water withdrawal can be sited where water-hungry thermal plants cannot.
- [Dry Cooling and Water-Scarce Siting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/dry-cooling-options.html): Air-cooled condensers trade some efficiency and footprint for near-elimination of cooling water, enabling siting where water is scarce.
- [Dual-Use and Brownfield Siting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/dual-use-and-brownfield-siting.html): Compact plants can reuse previously developed or brownfield land, avoiding disturbance of undeveloped ground.
- [Environmental Permitting: Water and Land Scope](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/environmental-permitting-water-land.html): Fusion plants are subject to standard environmental permitting for water, land, and discharge; compactness and low water reduce the scope, not the obligation.
- [Grid Interconnection Land](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/grid-interconnection-land.html): Substations and interconnection add land beyond the plant proper; co-located generation minimizes but does not eliminate it.
- [Habitat and Ecological Footprint](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/habitat-and-ecological-footprint.html): Compact, water-light plants disturb less habitat, but every project's ecological impact is site-specific and assessed directly.
- [Honest Gates and the Resource Case](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/honest-gates-and-the-resource-case.html): The four canonical burner gates are physics facts, not economics; stating them alongside the water and land advantages is what earns trust.
- [Land Disturbance During Construction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/land-disturbance-during-construction.html): A plant's largest one-time land impact is the construction phase; a compact plant disturbs correspondingly less ground.
- [Life-Cycle Water in Materials and Fuel](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/lifecycle-water-in-materials.html): A complete water account includes the water used to mine, process, and manufacture a plant's materials and fuel, not only its cooling.
- [Lithium for the Breeding Blanket](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/lithium-for-breeding-blanket.html): The breeder makes tritium by reacting neutrons with lithium; lithium is abundant, and the design question is enrichment and blanket engineering.
- [Lunar Helium-3 Context](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/lunar-helium-3-context.html): Lunar regolith is the only known large helium-3 reservoir; it is a long-horizon resource, described honestly without overclaiming.
- [Makeup Water and Treatment](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/makeup-water-and-treatment.html): Even low-water systems need some treated makeup water; the scale, not the existence, is what distinguishes generation technologies.
- [Material Recyclability and Circularity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/material-recyclability-and-circularity.html): Most plant materials are recyclable; the special case is activated components, handled as a characterized, decaying stream.
- [Material Resource Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/material-resource-overview.html): Both machines use a defined set of structural, magnet, and blanket materials; the honest question is intensity, sourcing, and recyclability.
- [MetroVolt Siting Context](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/metrovolt-siting-context.html): MetroVolt is the burner in a data-center housing, sited with the load it powers to shrink both water and transmission land.
- [Neutron Activation and Materials](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/neutron-activation-and-materials.html): Neutrons make nearby materials temporarily radioactive; the intensity scales with neutron fraction and is managed by material choice.
- [No Steam Cycle: How the Water Demand Disappears](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/direct-conversion-no-steam-cycle.html): Removing the turbine-condenser loop removes the single largest water demand in conventional thermal generation.
- [Noise, Light, and Local Impacts](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/noise-light-and-local-impacts.html): Beyond land area, a plant affects its surroundings through noise, lighting, and traffic; these are ordinary, manageable impacts.
- [Once-Through Versus Recirculating Cooling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/once-through-versus-recirculating-cooling.html): The two dominant thermal-plant cooling architectures trade water withdrawal against water consumption and ecological impact.
- [Power Density and Land Footprint](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/power-density-and-land-footprint.html): Power density — usable power per unit of land — is the honest lens for comparing how much ground a generation technology occupies.
- [REBCO Superconductor Materials](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/rebco-superconductor-materials.html): High-temperature REBCO tape enables the high fields both machines require; its supply chain is the material to watch, not a bulk commodity.
- [Resource Supply-Chain Resilience](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/resource-supply-chain-resilience.html): Fusion's fuel is abundant or bred, but its specialty materials have concentrated supply chains that are the real resilience question.
- [Setbacks and Exclusion Areas](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/setbacks-and-exclusion-areas.html): Regulatory setbacks and controlled areas are part of a plant's real land footprint and depend on its hazard profile.
- [Siting Criteria Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/siting-criteria-overview.html): Water, land, grid, security, and permitting jointly determine where a plant can be built; water-light, compact designs widen the options.
- [The Breeder's Thermal Load and Cooling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/breeder-thermal-load-and-cooling.html): The breeder (Hyperion) is a D-T machine that carries a genuine thermal load, so its water case is about cooling choice, not steam-cycle avoidance.
- [The Breeder-Bred Helium-3 Pathway](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/breeder-bred-helium-3-pathway.html): The breeder co-produces helium-3, providing a terrestrial pathway toward the burner's fuel, though far below fleet-scale demand.
- [The Burner's Residual Heat Loads](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/burner-residual-heat-loads.html): Direct conversion removes the steam cycle, but the burner still rejects heat from neutrons, magnets, and power electronics through closed loops.
- [The Helium-3 Supply Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/helium-3-supply-gate.html): The burner's helium-3 demand is roughly 400x domestic supply per commercial unit, a hard resource gate that shapes the whole deployment path.
- [Thermal Discharge and Water Quality](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/thermal-discharge-and-water-quality.html): Where any thermal water is returned to a source, its temperature and chemistry are regulated to protect aquatic ecosystems.
- [Thermoelectric Water Use: The Grid Baseline](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/thermoelectric-water-use-context.html): Thermoelectric power generation is among the largest categories of water withdrawal in industrialized economies, which is the backdrop for any water claim.
- [Tritium Breeding as a Design Lever](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-breeding-as-a-lever.html): The breeder makes its own tritium in a lithium blanket; the breeding ratio is a design lever, and self-sufficiency at the low end is an open question.
- [Tungsten and Plasma-Facing Materials](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tungsten-plasma-facing-materials.html): The surfaces facing the plasma must survive extreme heat and particle flux; tungsten is the leading choice, with a bounded, sourceable supply.
- [Water Withdrawal Versus Consumption](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/withdrawal-versus-consumption.html): A plant can withdraw a river yet consume little, or withdraw little yet evaporate most of it; using the wrong metric misleads.
- [Water in Magnet Cryogenics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/water-in-magnet-cryogenics.html): Superconducting magnets need refrigeration, and the cryoplant's heat rejection is a real but modest and closed-loop water term.
- [Water, Land, and Resource Profile: Summary](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/water-land-resource-profile-summary.html): A consolidated, honest view: the burner is water-light and land-light by architecture, the breeder is compact but cooling-dependent, and both carry stated gates.
- [Why Direct Energy Conversion Uses Little Water](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/why-direct-conversion-uses-little-water.html): The burner (Aegis / MetroVolt) recovers electricity from charged particles directly, so it never needs the large steam-cycle cooling loop that dominates thermal-plant water use.

### Fusion vs Alternatives
- [Activation Products vs Fission Products](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/activation-products-vs-fission-products.html): Neutron activation makes structures radioactive but leaves them chemically the same element; fission fragments the fuel into diverse, often long-lived isotopes.
- [Air Quality & Combustion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/air-quality-and-combustion.html): Combustion sources emit pollutants that harm health; fusion produces none of them at generation, sharing that clean-air property with renewables.
- [Availability: An Honest Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/availability-honest-gate.html): Firm power is only as firm as its uptime; the burner's simulated availability falls short of hyperscale Tier III, and Kronos says so.
- [Baseload & Firm Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/baseload-and-firm-supply.html): Baseload is the steady demand a grid always carries; firm clean sources like fusion can serve it without combustion.
- [Breeder 14 MeV Neutrons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/breeder-14-mev-neutron-context.html): The breeder's D-T reaction is strongly neutronic; those 14 MeV neutrons breed tritium and helium-3 and are managed by design.
- [Burner Neutron Fraction: Honest](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/burner-neutron-fraction-honest.html): The burner is low-neutron, not aneutronic: 5.44% of its energy arrives as neutrons, which is honestly stated and shapes shielding and cooling.
- [Capacity Factor Across Sources](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/capacity-factor-across-sources.html): A side-by-side of typical, public capacity factors shows why firm clean sources anchor a reliable low-carbon grid.
- [Capacity Factor Explained](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/capacity-factor-explained.html): Capacity factor is the fraction of nameplate power a source actually delivers over time; it separates firm sources from variable ones.
- [Co-Location with Data Centers](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/co-location-with-data-centers.html): The burner (MetroVolt) is housed to sit beside computing load, delivering firm clean power on-site — though availability remains an open gate.
- [Critical Minerals in Context](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/critical-minerals-in-context.html): Fusion uses lithium and specialty conductors but no continuously mined fuel; its critical-mineral demand is one-time and comparatively modest per unit energy.
- [Decommissioning Across Sources](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/decommissioning-across-sources.html): Every plant is eventually retired; fusion leaves activated structure that decays to recyclable levels, without long-lived spent fuel.
- [Dispatchability & Load Following](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/dispatchability-and-load-following.html): Dispatchable sources adjust output on command; fusion is designed to hold firm output and follow load, complementing variable renewables.
- [Energy Density & Fuel Mass](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/energy-density-and-fuel-mass.html): Fusion fuel carries extraordinary energy per unit mass, so a firm plant needs tiny fuel quantities compared to combustion.
- [Firm Power for Defense Sites](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/firm-power-for-defense-sites.html): The burner (Aegis) is housed for fixed defense installations needing resilient on-site firm power, with the same honest engineering gates.
- [Firm vs Variable Generation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/firm-vs-variable-generation.html): Variable sources follow the weather; firm sources follow demand. Understanding the difference explains where fusion fits.
- [Fuel Abundance Across Sources](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fuel-abundance-across-sources.html): Fusion fuel starts with deuterium from water — effectively unlimited — though the burner's helium-3 is scarce and gates that machine.
- [Fusion & Grid Storage](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-and-grid-storage.html): Storage and firm generation are partners, not substitutes; fusion covers the long-duration gaps that batteries alone cannot.
- [Fusion Complements Renewables](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-complements-renewables.html): Fusion is designed to firm a renewables-heavy grid, not to displace wind and solar; the two solve different halves of the problem.
- [Fusion Waste vs Fission Waste](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-waste-vs-fission-waste.html): Both produce radioactive material, but fusion's is activated structure that decays over engineering timescales, not long-lived fission products and actinides.
- [Fusion vs Alternatives: Scorecard](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/comparison-scorecard.html): A single honest scorecard of every source on the properties that matter for a clean grid — clean, firm, footprint — with fusion's gates in view.
- [Fusion vs Biomass](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-biomass.html): Biomass is dispatchable but combusts fuel and competes for land and water; fusion delivers firm output without combustion or crops.
- [Fusion vs Coal Generation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-coal-generation.html): Both deliver firm, dispatchable power; fusion is designed to do so without combustion, CO2, or particulate and sulfur emissions.
- [Fusion vs Fission Fuel Cycle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-fission-fuel-cycle.html): Fission depends on mining, enrichment, and spent-fuel management; fusion's cycle starts with water and breeds its own fuel in-plant.
- [Fusion vs Fission: An Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-fission-overview.html): Fusion and fission both split the atom's energy from mass, but differ in fuel, waste, and accident physics; both are firm and low-carbon.
- [Fusion vs Geothermal](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-geothermal.html): Geothermal is firm and clean where the crust cooperates; fusion aims to deliver the same firm clean role without geological constraints.
- [Fusion vs Hydropower](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-hydropower.html): Hydropower is firm, clean, and storable where geography allows; fusion offers firm clean power without dependence on rivers or reservoirs.
- [Fusion vs Natural Gas Generation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-natural-gas-generation.html): Gas is the modern firm-power workhorse; fusion aims to match its dispatchability while eliminating combustion CO2 and methane concerns.
- [Fusion vs Offshore Wind](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-offshore-wind.html): Offshore wind is steadier and higher-capacity than onshore but still weather-bound; fusion is designed as the firm complement.
- [Fusion vs Onshore Wind](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-onshore-wind.html): Onshore wind is a widely deployed clean workhorse but weather-driven; fusion targets the firm output that covers still, cold, high-demand periods.
- [Fusion vs Solar PV](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-vs-solar-pv.html): Solar is abundant, clean, and simple to run but variable; fusion is designed as the firm clean partner that covers the hours solar cannot.
- [Fusion's Complementary Role](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusions-complementary-role.html): Fusion is designed to complete a clean energy system, not to dominate it — the firm clean partner to abundant renewables and storage.
- [Fusion's Grid Reliability Role](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/grid-reliability-role.html): Reliability requires resources that are available at the moment of stress; fusion is designed to add firm clean capacity to a low-carbon grid.
- [Honest Limits & Open Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/honest-limits-and-open-gates.html): A plain summary of what fusion cannot yet claim: the machines are unbuilt, and the burner carries four specific, unsoftened engineering gates.
- [Land Footprint Across Sources](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/land-footprint-across-sources.html): Energy density sets land use: diffuse sources need large areas, while dense firm sources like fusion are compact per unit energy.
- [Lifecycle Emissions in Context](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/lifecycle-emissions-in-context.html): Every energy source carries some emissions from construction and materials; firm clean sources like fusion sit in the low-carbon band with wind, solar, and fission.
- [Low-Wind, Low-Sun Periods](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/low-wind-low-sun-periods.html): Extended calm, cloudy stretches are the hardest hours for a renewable grid; firm clean generation is designed to cover them.
- [Materials Footprint Across Sources](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/materials-footprint-across-sources.html): Every clean source needs materials; the honest comparison weighs steel and concrete against specialty inputs like magnets and rare earths.
- [No CO2 at the Point of Generation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-co2-at-the-point-of-generation.html): Fusion releases energy by fusing nuclei, not by burning carbon; there is no carbon dioxide emitted where the power is made.
- [No Meltdown Pathway](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-meltdown-pathway.html): A fusion plasma holds a tiny fuel inventory and stops the instant confinement is lost; there is no decay-heat meltdown pathway like a fission core.
- [No Particulates, SOx or NOx](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-particulate-or-sox-nox.html): Because fusion does not burn anything, it emits no fine particulates, sulfur oxides, or nitrogen oxides at generation.
- [No Runaway Reaction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-runaway-reaction-context.html): Fusion has no chain reaction; the plasma must be actively sustained, so any disturbance stops it rather than accelerating it.
- [Proliferation Context vs Fission](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/proliferation-context-vs-fission.html): Fusion uses no fissile fuel and produces no plutonium; its proliferation profile is narrower than fission's, though tritium is handled responsibly.
- [Recycling Activated Materials](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/recycling-activated-materials.html): Fusion's activated components are designed to decay to recyclable levels over engineering timescales, closing the material loop without deep geological disposal.
- [Seasonal Variability & Firmness](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/seasonal-variability-and-firmness.html): Renewable output swings with the seasons while demand often peaks in the opposite season; firm clean power bridges that mismatch.
- [Supply-Chain Materials in Context](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/supply-chain-materials-context.html): Fusion draws on specialty materials — superconductors, lithium, low-activation alloys — with real supply considerations, stated honestly against other sources.
- [Thermal Cycle vs Direct Conversion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/thermal-cycle-vs-direct-conversion.html): Most plants make heat then steam then power; the burner captures charged-particle energy directly, reducing the heat it must reject.
- [Transmission & Siting Footprint](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/transmission-and-siting-footprint.html): Compact firm sources can be sited near demand, reducing new long-distance transmission that diffuse renewables often require.
- [Water Use Across Sources](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/water-use-across-sources.html): Thermal plants use cooling water; fusion is thermal in the breeder but the burner's direct conversion sidesteps part of the thermal cycle.
- [What Firm Power Means](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/what-firm-power-means.html): Firm power is generation you can dispatch on demand; it is a different service from clean energy, and a grid needs both.
- [Why Firm Clean Power Matters](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/why-firm-clean-power-matters.html): A decarbonized grid still needs generation that is available on demand; fusion is being designed to fill that firm, clean role.

### Fuel & Sustainability
- [A Self-Sustaining Isotope Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/self-sustaining-isotope-supply.html): Running the breeder generates a renewable stream of tritium, helium-3, and neutrons — isotope products that sustain themselves from abundant inputs.
- [A Sustainable Fuel Cycle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/sustainable-fuel-cycle.html): Sustainability here means a fuel cycle whose inputs are abundant, whose loop is closed, and whose operation does not deplete a scarce resource.
- [Breeding Ratio 1.1 — Near Self-Sufficiency](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/breeding-ratio-1-1.html): A breeding ratio of 1.1 keeps a single machine fueled with a modest margin, prioritizing engineering simplicity over rapid fuel accumulation.
- [Breeding Ratio 1.5 — Comfortable Margin](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/breeding-ratio-1-5.html): A breeding ratio of 1.5 gives a substantial fuel surplus, enough to absorb losses comfortably and to help start additional machines.
- [Breeding Ratio 1.8 — Strong Margin](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/breeding-ratio-1-8.html): A breeding ratio of 1.8 maximizes fuel surplus and fleet-growth potential, at the cost of the most demanding blanket engineering.
- [Compared To Battery And Rare-Earth Minerals](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/compare-critical-minerals.html): Fusion's fuel does not draw on the concentrated critical-mineral supply chains that constrain many clean-energy technologies.
- [Compared To Fossil Fuel Supply Chains](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/compare-fossil-supply-chains.html): Fossil energy depends on continuous extraction and transport of large fuel masses; fusion runs on a tiny mass of fuel drawn from water.
- [Compared To Uranium Mining And Enrichment](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/compare-uranium-fuel-cycle.html): The fusion fuel cycle avoids uranium's ore mining, enrichment, and long-lived spent fuel, and it produces no fissile material.
- [Deuterium Abundance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/deuterium-abundance.html): Deuterium's natural concentration in water is fixed and well measured, which makes the size of the fuel reservoir straightforward to reason about.
- [Deuterium From Seawater](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/deuterium-from-seawater.html): Every fusion reaction in the breeder (Hyperion) starts with deuterium, a stable hydrogen isotope present in ordinary seawater.
- [Energy Density Of Fusion Fuel](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/energy-density-of-fusion-fuel.html): Fusion releases millions of times more energy per unit mass than chemical fuels, which is why the required fuel mass is so small.
- [Energy Security Through Abundance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/energy-security-through-abundance.html): When fuel is universally available and bred on site, energy security shifts from controlling supply to building capacity.
- [Fuel And Sustainability Glossary](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fuel-and-sustainability-glossary.html): Definitions of the key fuel-cycle and sustainability terms used across these pages, stated plainly and honestly.
- [Fuel Logistics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fuel-logistics.html): Because the fuel mass is tiny and partly bred on site, moving and storing fusion fuel is a small-scale operation.
- [Fuel Purity Requirements](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fuel-purity-requirements.html): Fusion plasmas are sensitive to impurities, so fuel must be prepared and kept clean — a handling requirement, not a supply constraint.
- [Fuel Reserves Versus Global Demand](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/reserves-versus-demand.html): Setting the deuterium reservoir against global energy demand shows why the supply is described as effectively unlimited.
- [Fuel Storage And Handling](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fuel-storage-and-handling.html): The stable fuel components are easy to store; tritium is handled with containment and accounting because it is radioactive and mobile.
- [Fuel-Cycle Sustainability Metrics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fuel-cycle-sustainability-metrics.html): A short set of physical measures captures why the fusion fuel cycle is sustainable: input abundance, loop closure, and waste class.
- [Fusion Fuel Versus Fission And Fossil](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fuel-vs-fission-vs-fossil.html): A side-by-side look at where each fuel comes from, how long it lasts, and what it leaves behind — comparing fuel cycles only.
- [Helium-3 Bred In Situ](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/helium3-bred-in-situ.html): The breeder (Hyperion) produces helium-3 as part of its own fuel cycle, so the isotope is made on site rather than mined.
- [Helium-3 Recovery And Purification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/helium3-recovery.html): Helium-3 accumulates from decaying tritium and is separated from ordinary helium and other gases before use.
- [Helium-3 Scarcity In Context](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/helium3-scarcity-context.html): Helium-3 is one of the rarest useful isotopes on Earth; understanding that scarcity explains why breeding it changes the picture.
- [Helium-3 Without Mining](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/helium3-no-mining.html): Because helium-3 is bred from lithium and hydrogen isotopes, the breeder needs no terrestrial or lunar mining to obtain it.
- [Lithium For The Breeding Blanket](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/lithium-for-breeding.html): Tritium is bred when blanket lithium absorbs fusion neutrons; lithium is abundant, widely distributed, and used in modest quantities per plant.
- [Lithium Recycling In The Blanket](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/lithium-recycling.html): Lithium in the breeding blanket is not destroyed by breeding tritium; it can be recovered and recycled, keeping the input demand small.
- [Lithium-6 Versus Lithium-7](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/lithium-6-vs-lithium-7.html): The two natural lithium isotopes breed tritium by different reactions, and their balance is a design lever for the breeding blanket.
- [Longevity Of Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fuel-supply-longevity.html): At any plausible rate of global energy use, the deuterium in the ocean represents a fuel supply lasting far beyond human timescales.
- [No Fissile Fuel In The Cycle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-fissile-fuel.html): Fusion fuel contains no uranium or plutonium, so the fuel cycle offers no pathway to weapons-usable fissile material.
- [No Fuel-Supply Geopolitics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-fuel-geopolitics.html): Because the fuel comes from seawater and is bred on site, fusion removes the resource-control dynamics that shape conventional energy.
- [No Mining Footprint For Fuel](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/no-fuel-mining-footprint.html): Neither the deuterium nor the bred helium-3 requires ore extraction, so the fuel cycle carries no mine, tailings, or excavation footprint.
- [Recovering Tritium From The Blanket](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/blanket-tritium-recovery.html): Tritium bred in the lithium blanket must be extracted efficiently and returned to the plasma for the fuel cycle to close.
- [Separating Deuterium](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/deuterium-extraction.html): Deuterium is concentrated from water using mature industrial chemistry — no mining, no exotic reagents, and no radioactive input.
- [The Breeder-Burner Fuel Link](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/breeder-burner-fuel-link.html): The breeder (Hyperion) makes helium-3; the burner (Aegis / MetroVolt) uses it — two machines joined by a shared fuel product.
- [The Closed Fuel Cycle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/closed-fuel-cycle.html): A closed fuel cycle regenerates its own fuel internally, so the plant depends on abundant external inputs only, not on a continuing fuel supply.
- [The Deuterium-Helium-3 Fuel Cycle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/dhe3-fuel-cycle.html): The burner (Aegis / MetroVolt) fuses deuterium with helium-3, a reaction whose main products are charged particles rather than neutrons.
- [The Deuterium-To-Hydrogen Ratio](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/deuterium-hydrogen-ratio.html): The ratio of deuterium to ordinary hydrogen in ocean water is a precisely defined standard, which anchors any reasoning about the fuel supply.
- [The Deuterium-Tritium Fuel Cycle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/dt-fuel-cycle.html): The breeder (Hyperion) runs on deuterium and tritium, breeding its own tritium so the cycle closes with only water-derived and abundant inputs.
- [The Earth-Moon Fuel Picture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/earth-moon-fuel-picture.html): Helium-3 can come from breeding on Earth and, over the longer term, from lunar sources — an honest look at both routes.
- [The Energy Cost Of Separation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/deuterium-extraction-energy.html): Concentrating deuterium takes energy, but that input is a tiny fraction of the energy the fuel later releases in fusion.
- [The Fuel Supply Chain End To End](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fuel-supply-chain-end-to-end.html): From ocean water to fusion and back to bred fuel, the complete chain has few steps and no extractive bottleneck.
- [The Neutron Economy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/neutron-economy.html): Every fusion neutron is a resource: it can breed tritium, multiply into more neutrons, or be lost, and balancing this budget sets the breeding ratio.
- [The Ocean As A Fuel Reservoir](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/ocean-hydrogen-reservoir.html): The world ocean is an enormous, self-renewing store of hydrogen, and the deuterium within it is the practical source of primary fusion fuel.
- [The Water Cycle And Fuel](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/water-cycle-and-fuel.html): Drawing deuterium from water does not consume water in any meaningful sense; the separated water returns to the hydrological cycle.
- [Tritium Breeding Ratio As A Design Lever](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-breeding-ratio.html): The tritium breeding ratio measures how much tritium a machine makes per unit consumed; the breeder studies it across values of 1.1, 1.5, and 1.8.
- [Tritium Decays To Helium-3](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-decay-to-helium3.html): Tritium is radioactive with a 12.3-year half-life, and its only decay product is stable helium-3 — the physical basis for breeding the isotope.
- [Tritium Inventory And Decay](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-inventory-and-decay.html): Tritium's 12.3-year half-life means a working inventory must be managed actively, but it also guarantees no long-lived fuel legacy.
- [Tritium Self-Sufficiency](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/tritium-self-sufficiency.html): A deuterium-tritium plant must breed all the tritium it burns; self-sufficiency is what makes the fuel cycle closed and independent of external supply.
- [What Bred Helium-3 Can Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/helium3-uses-supplied.html): Helium-3 has uses with no easy substitute; a breeder that makes it in situ can supply those needs from a renewable source.

### The Vision
- [A Day in 2050](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/a-day-in-2050.html): A deliberately illustrative sketch of ordinary life on a clean, firm-powered grid — offered as a picture, not a prediction.
- [Abundant Clean Energy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/abundant-clean-energy.html): If fusion delivers firm power at scale, energy stops being the scarce input that everything else is rationed against.
- [Cities That Breathe](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/cities-that-breathe.html): Freed from combustion and its footprint, cities can weave nature back through the built environment rather than paving it out.
- [Clean-Air Cities](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/clean-air-cities.html): Most urban air pollution is combustion; replacing the burning with clean electricity clears the air people breathe every day.
- [Computing and Discovery](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/computing-and-discovery.html): Clean power and large-scale computation form a loop: energy runs the models, and the models accelerate the science, including fusion itself.
- [Energy Without Emissions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/energy-without-emissions.html): The core promise of fusion is decoupling energy from the smokestack: capability that does not add carbon or combustion pollution to the air.
- [Energy and Biodiversity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/energy-and-biodiversity.html): Habitat loss and climate change are the two great pressures on wild life; clean, compact, firm energy eases both at once.
- [Energy and Isotopes for Medicine](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/energy-for-medicine.html): Beyond electricity, fusion machines produce neutrons and isotopes that medicine relies on — a health dividend alongside the clean-power one.
- [Energy and the Good Life](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/energy-and-the-good-life.html): Abundant clean power is not an end in itself; it is what lets people live well and live closer to nature at the same time.
- [Energy for Everyone](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/energy-for-everyone.html): A billion people still lack reliable electricity; compact firm clean generation could extend modern energy without repeating the fossil path.
- [Firm Power for a Renewable Grid](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/firm-power-for-a-renewable-grid.html): The hardest part of a clean grid is the last increment of reliability; firm fusion is designed to supply exactly that.
- [From Scarcity to Abundance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/from-scarcity-to-abundance.html): The mindset shift the vision asks for: treating energy as something that can be abundant and clean, rather than a fixed budget to be fought over.
- [Fusion and the Reach into Space](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/fusion-and-space.html): The same fuels and physics that power a clean planet also point outward — helium-3, deep-space power, and a lunar link that closes back onto Earth.
- [Industry Without Smoke](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/industry-without-smoke.html): Heavy industry runs on high-temperature heat that has meant combustion; clean electricity and clean fuels can supply that heat without the smokestack.
- [Oceans and Fusion](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/oceans-and-fusion.html): The ocean absorbs our carbon and our heat; ending combustion and easing the pressure on rivers gives marine systems room to stabilize.
- [Powering Advanced Intelligence, Cleanly](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/powering-advanced-ai.html): Large-scale computation is becoming a defining human capability — and its growing appetite for power can be met without a growing emissions bill.
- [Resilience and Energy Security](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/resilience-and-security.html): Energy made from abundant, widely available fuel and produced near where it is used is harder to disrupt and less bound to geopolitics.
- [Restoring Nature](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/restoring-nature.html): The active repair of ecosystems — forests, wetlands, soils — becomes possible at scale when the energy to do the work is clean and abundant.
- [Restoring the Carbon Balance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/restoring-the-carbon-balance.html): Cutting emissions to zero stops the problem growing; abundant clean energy is what makes pulling legacy carbon back out affordable in energy terms.
- [Rewilding and Land](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/rewilding-and-land.html): Compact generation returns land to nature: the smaller the footprint of power, the more of the map can be left wild.
- [The Electrified World](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/the-electrified-world.html): The cleanest path for most of the economy is to electrify it and make the electricity clean; abundant firm power is what makes that switch complete.
- [The Endgame: A Balanced World](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/the-endgame-a-balanced-world.html): The destination is not a utopia but a balance — an advanced society and a recovering planet, held together by clean firm power.
- [The Firm-Clean Pair](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/the-firm-clean-pair.html): Fusion and renewables are complements, not rivals: variable sources do the bulk decarbonization, firm clean power closes the reliability gap.
- [The Fuel That Doesn’t Run Out](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/the-fuel-that-doesnt-run-out.html): Fusion’s fuels are drawn from water and bred in the machine, not dug from a mine — a supply that does not deplete on any human timescale.
- [The Generational Project](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/the-generational-project.html): Building the clean-energy foundation is the work of more than one career; naming that honestly is part of taking it seriously.
- [The Healed Planet](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/the-healed-planet.html): The endgame is not merely lower emissions but a biosphere given the energy and the room to recover.
- [The Long Horizon](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/the-long-horizon.html): This is a hundred-year project stated honestly: near-term steps that are concrete, a far endgame that is aspirational, and no pretense that they are the same thing.
- [The Post-Combustion Era](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/the-post-combustion-era.html): The through-line of the vision is the end of burning things for energy — a civilizational shift as large as the one that started with fire.
- [The Vision](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/the-vision.html): The world fusion could help build: an advanced society powered cleanly while the living planet is given room to heal.
- [Water Abundance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/water-abundance.html): Fresh water is scarce mainly because making it costs energy; abundant clean power turns desalination and reuse from last resorts into everyday tools.
- [What We Don’t Claim](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/ehs/honest-vision-what-we-dont-claim.html): A vision is only trustworthy if its limits are as clear as its hopes; this page states plainly what Kronos does not promise.
